messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: p99 SLO breach detected for /v1/streaming/generate (hosted-prod). p95 elevated. Rolling 5m window shows p99=4.2s (SLO=1.5s). Errors: increased streaming stall rate. Trigger: auth/config fetch latency spike.

sara: seeing this on dashboards now, thanks bot. who is oncall?

devon: i'm oncall. saw alert 2m ago. ingest/edge traffic looks normal but auth token fetch latencies spiking to 800-1200ms.

emily: confirm — tracing shows control-plane calls: configfetch and auth-token-store are the hot paths. sample traces: ````
trace 1: /v1/streaming -> inference-gateway -> controlplane/auth (600ms) -> token-store (420ms) -> model-proxy
trace 2: /v1/streaming -> configfetch (1.1s) -> feature-flag eval -> fallback path
````

raj: pulling DB metrics now. tokenstore RDS read latency jumped 5x, CPU spiked on tokenstore pod set. I see increased contention on index idx_tokens_last_used.

ken: any recent deploys to tokenstore or controlplane?

devon: nothing in the last 3 hours per deploy-bot. config flags changed ~45m ago (pm-anna), but that was for a small canary.

pm-anna: I rolled out feature flag "auth-token-cache-v2" to 10% at 09:12 PDT. Was intended to reduce load.

emily: odd — traces show more misses vs hits on the new cache; cache warming issue maybe causing more backend reads. Miss rate jumped from 8% -> 62% post-rollout.

raj: reproducing locally: cache key normalization bug — keys include ephemeral session id in some codepaths -> cache miss storm. pushing hotfix to disable that normalization.

devon: mitigation proposal: 1) throttle incoming streaming routes to reduce tokenstore QPS 2) rollback feature flag to 0% 3) enable configfetch fallback (use cached config for 5m) 4) route high-latency requests to dedicated-backup pool (lower throughput but isolated).

ken: +1. Also increase streaming client timeout to avoid client-side retry storms.

ops-bot: POST /v1/admin/traffic-shape -> applied 20% shed on non-critical streaming routes.

devon: rolling rollback of auth-token-cache-v2 to 0%. doing canary at 0% -> 0% across all regions.

pm-anna: ack, rolling back now.

emily: after rollback start: cache miss rate trending down, tokenstore p95 drop from 420ms -> 110ms over 30s. p99 trending down too.

raj: tokenstore CPU dropping, replication lag within normal. index contention relieved. patch for normalization is queued for release but not required if we keep old behavior.

devon: routing change: switched ~12% of streaming sessions to dedicated-backup pool (no KV caching) to reduce tail. p99 for routed sessions is higher but overall cluster p99 improved.

customer-ops: Customer impact check: telemetry shows ~3.4% of streaming sessions saw stalls >2s during the peak (09:18-09:28 PDT). Affected customers: 6 orgs with high throughput. No order-of-magnitude data loss. Will prepare customer notices if impact persists >30m.

ken: should we open a SEV follow-up? I think this stays SEV until p99 < 1.5s for 15m.

devon: agreed. oncall handoff: i'll keep ownership for next 30m then hand to raj for postmortem and action items (db index + codefix). raj you ok to take?

raj: yep, i'll own the post-incident. next steps: revert cache rollout permanently until fix, add unit + integration test for key normalization, add circuit-breaker on tokenstore reads at client side, add telemetry for miss spikes.

emily: monitoring: added temporary alert for configfetch miss-rate > 20% and tokenstore miss storm.

ops-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: mitigation steps applied. p99 reduced to 1.6s and trending. continuing to monitor.

devon: good work team. i'll update status page and keep customer-ops looped. preparing handoff notes.

customer-ops: drafting customer-facing note: brief summary, mitigations, ETA for patch (est 24-48h).

pm-anna: sorry for the rollout chaos — will coordinate dark-launch testing next time.

raj: adding postmortem owners: raj (engineer), emily (observability), pm-anna (product), devon (oncall timeline).

devon: last check: p99 now 1.3s. marking majority mitigated. will close SEV if stable 15m.

incident-bot: RESOLVED: SLO back within threshold. p99=1.2s, p95=0.45s. Incident duration: ~18m.

sara: thanks all. please leave follow-up action items in the postmortem doc. :thumbsup:
